title: Ransomware attack encrypts regional hospital network
description: At 03:40 staff reported that electronic health record terminals displayed a ransom note. Over 1,200 endpoints and file servers were encrypted by a double-extortion ransomware strain. Radiology, lab systems and e-prescribing went offline and the emergency department diverted ambulances. Attackers claimed to have exfiltrated 400 GB of patient data.

actions: Isolated all network segments and disabled VPN and remote access
Activated downtime procedures with paper charting and ambulance diversion
Engaged incident response retainer and notified FBI and HHS
Rebuilt Active Directory from offline backups and reset all privileged credentials
Restored clinical systems in priority order from immutable backups
Issued breach notifications to affected patients within 60 days
past_response.outcome: Critical clinical systems restored in 9 days; no ransom paid; ambulance diversion lifted after 36 hours.
lessons_learned: Immutable, offline backups were decisive in avoiding ransom payment
Downtime procedures must be drilled quarterly
MFA was missing on a legacy VPN appliance used for initial access

title: DDoS attack takes down city emergency services portal
description: A volumetric DDoS peaking at 480 Gbps targeted the municipal website, non-emergency 311 line web gateway and online emergency alert sign-up page during a heat advisory. A hacktivist group claimed responsibility. Core 911 telephony was unaffected but public information channels were unavailable for six hours.

actions: Rerouted traffic through upstream ISP scrubbing and CDN DDoS protection
Published critical heat advisory information via social media and radio
Applied geo-blocking and rate limiting on application endpoints
Coordinated with CISA and ISP for attribution and traffic analysis
past_response.outcome: Services restored in 6 hours; permanent always-on DDoS protection contracted.
lessons_learned: Always-on scrubbing is required for public safety communication channels
Maintain out-of-band public communication channels independent of city web infrastructure

title: Unauthorized access to water treatment SCADA system
description: An operator observed the HMI cursor moving on its own and the sodium hydroxide setpoint being raised from 100 ppm to 11,100 ppm. Access was traced to a remote desktop tool with a shared password on an internet-exposed workstation. The operator reverted the change before chemical levels reached the distribution system.

actions: Disconnected remote access tools and isolated the OT network from IT
Placed chemical dosing into manual control with on-site verification
Increased water quality sampling frequency to hourly
Notified state drinking water regulator, FBI and CISA
Replaced shared credentials and deployed MFA for all remote OT access
past_response.outcome: No contaminated water reached consumers; OT network segmentation completed within 30 days.
lessons_learned: Shared passwords and unmanaged remote desktop tools are unacceptable in OT environments
Operator vigilance and manual overrides prevented harm
Automated setpoint bounds checking should block unsafe values

title: Customer database breach via SQL injection
description: Threat intelligence found a dump of 2.3 million customer records including names, emails, hashed passwords and partial card data on a criminal forum. Investigation revealed a SQL injection vulnerability in a legacy order-tracking endpoint exploited over three weeks.

actions: Took the vulnerable endpoint offline and deployed WAF virtual patch
Forced password resets for all customer accounts
Engaged forensic firm and notified card brands and data protection authority within 72 hours
Offered credit monitoring to affected customers
Commissioned code audit of all legacy endpoints
past_response.outcome: Regulatory notification met the 72-hour deadline; fine reduced due to cooperation.
lessons_learned: Legacy endpoints must be included in regular penetration tests
Database activity monitoring would have detected bulk extraction earlier

title: Supply chain compromise of IT management software update
description: A vendor disclosed that a signed update of its IT monitoring agent contained a backdoor. The update had been deployed to 3,400 servers across 14 state agencies. Beaconing to attacker infrastructure was confirmed on 60 hosts, and lateral movement was observed in two agencies.

actions: Blocked known C2 domains and IPs at all perimeter firewalls
Uninstalled the compromised agent and isolated hosts with confirmed beaconing
Hunted for persistence and lateral movement using vendor-provided IOCs
Rotated service account and domain credentials across affected agencies
Established joint incident command with CISA and vendor
past_response.outcome: Threat evicted after 5 weeks; two agencies rebuilt their domains from scratch.
lessons_learned: Software bill of materials and vendor risk assessments are essential
Egress filtering from servers would have blocked beaconing

title: Major river flooding inundates downtown and residential districts
description: Five days of heavy rain combined with snowmelt pushed the Cedar River 4.2 m above flood stage. Two levees were overtopped, flooding 3,800 homes, the downtown business district and a wastewater treatment plant. Three people died in vehicles attempting to cross flooded roads.

actions: Issued mandatory evacuation orders for flood zones using emergency alert system
Opened 6 shelters with Red Cross and deployed National Guard high-water vehicles
Closed 40 road segments and deployed turn-around-don't-drown barriers
Sandbagged critical facilities and deployed temporary flood barriers at the hospital
Issued boil-water advisory after wastewater plant failure
Requested federal disaster declaration
past_response.outcome: Over 18,000 residents evacuated; federal declaration approved in 4 days.
lessons_learned: Road closure enforcement must begin before water reaches roads
Critical facilities in floodplain need permanent flood protection

title: Magnitude 6.8 earthquake strikes metropolitan area
description: A shallow M6.8 earthquake caused partial collapse of 14 unreinforced masonry buildings, ruptured gas mains sparking 22 fires, and damaged a freeway overpass. 41 fatalities and over 900 injuries were reported. Power was lost to 300,000 customers and cell networks were congested.

actions: Activated emergency operations center and urban search and rescue teams
Shut off gas to affected zones and prioritized fire suppression
Established casualty collection points and field triage
Conducted rapid structural safety assessments (red/yellow/green tagging)
Deployed mobile cell towers and satellite communications
Opened mass care shelters and family reunification centers
past_response.outcome: 37 people rescued from rubble; utilities restored within 10 days.
lessons_learned: Pre-staged USAR caches accelerated rescue
Automatic seismic gas shutoff valves reduce fire ignitions
Redundant satellite communications are essential when cell networks congest

title: Wind-driven wildfire threatens suburban communities
description: A wildfire ignited by downed power lines spread at 2 km/h under 90 km/h wind gusts, burning 12,000 hectares in 18 hours. It destroyed 540 structures and forced evacuation of 35,000 residents. Smoke caused hazardous air quality across the region.

actions: Issued zone-based evacuation orders and warnings via alerts and door-to-door notification
Implemented contraflow on primary evacuation routes
Requested mutual aid strike teams and air tankers
Utility executed public safety power shutoff in adjacent high-risk circuits
Opened evacuation centers with air filtration and animal shelters
Issued air quality health advisories
past_response.outcome: No fatalities; containment reached in 9 days.
lessons_learned: Pre-defined evacuation zones enabled clear messaging
Earlier preemptive power shutoffs could have prevented ignition

title: Category 4 hurricane landfall on coastal region
description: A Category 4 hurricane made landfall with 230 km/h winds and 3.5 m storm surge. Surge flooded barrier islands and coastal towns, and 1.8 million customers lost power. Two bridges to barrier islands were damaged, stranding 4,000 residents who did not evacuate.

actions: Issued mandatory evacuations 48 hours before landfall for surge zones
Pre-positioned utility crews, fuel, water and meals outside impact zone
Evacuated vulnerable patients from coastal hospitals and nursing homes
Conducted post-landfall search and rescue by boat and helicopter
Established points of distribution for water, food and ice
Deployed temporary causeway to reconnect barrier island
past_response.outcome: Power restored to 95% in 12 days; 900 people rescued post-landfall.
lessons_learned: Evacuation compliance needs targeted messaging for vulnerable populations
Generator fuel logistics for critical facilities must be pre-contracted

title: Severe winter ice storm causes prolonged outages
description: Freezing rain accumulating 25 mm of ice collapsed transmission lines and trees, leaving 420,000 customers without power in sub-zero temperatures. Carbon monoxide poisonings rose from improper generator use and roads were impassable for 3 days.

actions: Opened warming centers with transport for vulnerable residents
Issued carbon monoxide safety messaging in multiple languages
Prioritized power restoration for hospitals, water plants and shelters
Deployed plows and National Guard for welfare checks
Coordinated mutual aid line crews from neighboring states
past_response.outcome: Power restored in 8 days; 12 CO-poisoning deaths prompted new outreach programs.
lessons_learned: CO safety messaging must start before the storm hits
Registry of medically dependent residents speeds welfare checks

title: Cascading regional power grid failure during heat wave
description: During a 46 degree C heat wave a transmission line fault triggered cascading trips that blacked out 3.2 million customers. Traffic signals, water pumping stations and hospital HVAC systems failed and heat-related emergency calls tripled.

actions: Grid operator performed black-start restoration in priority sequence
Deployed generators to hospitals, water pumping and dialysis centers
Opened cooling centers and paused utility disconnections
Deployed police to major intersections for traffic control
Issued conservation appeals once partial service was restored
past_response.outcome: Full restoration in 30 hours; 14 heat-related deaths.
lessons_learned: Critical facility generator testing under load must be verified annually
Cooling centers need backup power

title: Water main break and contamination triggers boil-water order
description: A 1.2 m transmission main ruptured, dropping pressure below 20 psi across the eastside zone. Post-break sampling detected E. coli in two locations. 180,000 residents, three hospitals and 40 schools were affected.

actions: Issued boil-water advisory via alerts, media and door hangers
Isolated the break and flushed and chlorinated affected mains
Distributed bottled water at 8 points of distribution
Coordinated with hospitals on alternate water supplies
Collected confirmation samples for two consecutive days before lifting advisory
past_response.outcome: Advisory lifted after 5 days; no confirmed illness cluster.
lessons_learned: Pre-scripted multilingual boil-water messages accelerated notification
Aging transmission mains need condition assessment

title: Highway bridge structural failure during rush hour
description: A 45 m span of a steel girder highway bridge collapsed during morning rush hour, sending 6 vehicles and a bus into the ravine. 10 people were injured and a ruptured gas line on the bridge created a fire hazard.

actions: Dispatched technical rope rescue and structural collapse teams
Shut off the gas line and established hazard exclusion zone
Closed the corridor and activated detour routes with traffic management
Initiated inspection of all bridges of similar design statewide
Preserved scene for NTSB investigation
past_response.outcome: All occupants rescued; no fatalities; replacement bridge opened in 11 months.
lessons_learned: Fracture-critical bridges need accelerated inspection intervals
Utilities attached to bridges require automatic shutoff capability

title: Regional telecom outage disables 911 call routing
description: A failed router software update at a carrier caused a 7-hour outage of 911 call routing to four public safety answering points. Callers received busy signals and an estimated 900 emergency calls failed to connect.

actions: Published alternate 10-digit emergency numbers and text-to-911 guidance
Staffed fire stations and police stations as walk-in emergency reporting points
Carrier rolled back the software update and rerouted via backup trunks
Filed outage reports with telecom regulator
Conducted callback to abandoned 911 call numbers after restoration
past_response.outcome: Service restored after 7 hours; regulator fined carrier for missing redundancy.
lessons_learned: PSAPs need diverse carrier routing
Pre-approved public messaging for 911 outages saves critical time

title: Active shooter incident at shopping mall
description: A lone gunman opened fire in the crowded food court during holiday shopping. Police received over 200 calls in 4 minutes. 5 people were killed and 11 wounded before the suspect was neutralized 7 minutes after the first call.

actions: First arriving officers formed contact team and engaged the threat
Rescue task forces with EMS entered warm zones to treat casualties
Established unified command, staging area and casualty collection point
Evacuated and searched the mall, and established a family reunification center
Coordinated hospital surge notifications and victim identification
Delivered public information updates through a single joint information center
past_response.outcome: Threat neutralized in 7 minutes; all wounded transported within 45 minutes.
lessons_learned: Rescue task force training reduced time to treatment
Reunification center location should be pre-planned for major venues

title: Train derailment releases toxic chlorine gas
description: A freight train derailed and breached a tank car carrying 80 tons of chlorine, creating a toxic plume drifting toward residential areas. 60 people reported respiratory symptoms and two rail workers were hospitalized in critical condition.

actions: Established hot, warm and cold zones and issued shelter-in-place orders downwind
Evacuated the 1.5 km radius upwind and crosswind
Deployed hazmat teams to plug the breach and apply water curtains
Set up decontamination at hospitals and field sites
Deployed air monitoring networks and published readings
Coordinated with railroad, EPA and chemical manufacturer CHEMTREC
past_response.outcome: Leak stopped in 14 hours; residents returned after 3 days of air monitoring.
lessons_learned: Plume modeling must drive zone-based shelter-in-place messaging
Hospitals need advance notice for decontamination surge

title: Crowd crush at stadium concert exit
description: After a concert, a surge toward a narrow exit concourse created a crowd crush. 32 people were injured, 4 critically, and emergency responders had trouble accessing the concourse through dense crowds.

actions: Stopped the performance of the after-show and used PA announcements to halt egress
Opened all emergency exits and redirected crowd flow
Established medical triage on the field level
Coordinated transit to hold trains and prevent platform overcrowding
Commissioned crowd dynamics review of venue egress
past_response.outcome: No fatalities; venue redesigned exit routes and added crowd density monitoring.
lessons_learned: Real-time crowd density monitoring can detect crush precursors
Pre-agreed show-stop procedures must be communicated to performers

title: Foodborne illness outbreak linked to school lunch program
description: Over 48 hours, 210 students across 9 schools reported vomiting and diarrhea. Lab testing confirmed Salmonella traced to pre-cut produce from a single supplier. 14 children were hospitalized and none died.

actions: Removed and quarantined the implicated produce from all district kitchens
Health department conducted case interviews and lab testing
Issued parent notifications with symptom guidance
Coordinated recall with supplier and food safety regulator
Enhanced cafeteria sanitation and temporary menu substitutions
past_response.outcome: Outbreak contained within 1 week; supplier recall issued in 3 states.
lessons_learned: Supplier traceability records enabled rapid source identification
Parent communication templates reduced confusion
